name: Queen's Gambit
description: Offers the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre, trading a wing pawn for lasting central control and development.
recommended_response: The Queen's Gambit Declined (2...e6) is the most solid reply; accepting with 2...dxc4 hands White a free tempo to reclaim the pawn.

name: King's Gambit
description: A Romantic-era pawn sacrifice that rips open the f-file and the a7-g1 diagonal for a rapid kingside attack.
recommended_response: King's Gambit Declined (2...Bc5) sidesteps the sharpest theory while keeping a safe, comfortable game.

name: Evans Gambit
description: Gives up the b-pawn to gain time on the bishop and grab a big centre before Black finishes developing.
recommended_response: 4...Bxb4 5.c3 Ba5 keeps the extra pawn while staying flexible; 4...Bb6 declines and avoids the sharpest lines entirely.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
description: Sacrifices a pawn against the Sicilian for a quick lead in development and open lines toward Black's king.
recommended_response: 3...Nf6 or the solid 3...d3 declines; accepting with 3...dxc3 is playable but requires careful defence.

name: Danish Gambit
description: Offers two pawns in a row to fling both bishops onto open diagonals aimed straight at Black's king.
recommended_response: 3...d5! strikes back in the centre immediately and is the most reliable antidote.

name: Scotch Gambit
description: Trades the d-pawn for quick piece development, reaching Italian-style attacking positions a tempo up on the normal lines.
recommended_response: 5...Bc5 or 5...Nf6 develop naturally and meet White's lead in development head-on.

name: Stafford Gambit
description: A trappy pawn sacrifice out of the Petrov, banking on rapid development and tactics to punish an unwary opponent.
recommended_response: 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3 (or 5.e5) returns the extra pawn's worth of comfort and steers clear of the sharpest traps.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
description: Gives up a pawn in the opening to blast open lines for both minor pieces and the queen against a still-uncastled king.
recommended_response: 3...Nf6 (the Bogoljubov Defence) or simply holding the pawn with careful development neutralises most of the tricks.

name: Budapest Gambit
description: Black offers a pawn to lure White's d-pawn forward, then hunts it back with active piece play around e4/e5.
recommended_response: 3.dxe5 Ng4 4.Bf4 (or 4.Nf3) is the main line; 3.Nf3 sidesteps the gambit's sharpest tries entirely.

name: Benko Gambit
description: Trades a queenside pawn for long-term pressure down the open a- and b-files against White's queenside.
recommended_response: 4.cxb5 a6 5.bxa6 (accepting) is the main test; 4.Nf3 or 4.a4 decline and aim to just hold the extra pawn.

name: Modern Benoni
description: Not a true pawn sacrifice, but an aggressive space-for-activity trade: Black cedes central space for a dynamic, unbalanced middlegame.
recommended_response: 6.Nc3 exd5 7.cxd5 with a big White centre is the main tabiya; a well-timed ...b5 break is Black's standard counterplay.

name: Englund Gambit
description: An immediate, slightly dubious pawn sacrifice aiming to drag White out of prepared Queen's Pawn theory into a scrappy tactical fight.
recommended_response: 2.dxe5 Nc6 3.Nf3 is the safest way to keep the extra pawn without walking into the known tricks.

name: Albin Countergambit
description: Black answers the Queen's Gambit with a countergambit, using the advanced d-pawn to cramp White's position after dxe5 d4.
recommended_response: 3.dxe5 d4 4.Nf3 (avoiding 4.e3's traps) is the modern main line.

name: Marshall Attack
description: A deeply prepared pawn sacrifice in the Ruy Lopez, trading the d-pawn for a long-lasting initiative and attacking chances against White's king.
recommended_response: The Anti-Marshall (8.a4 or 8.h3) sidesteps the gambit entirely and is the most common practical try for White.

name: Fried Liver Attack
description: A knight sacrifice straight out of the Two Knights Defence that drags Black's king into the open for a violent early attack.
recommended_response: Declining with 4...d5 (rather than 4...Nxd5-style play) or simply 4...Bc5 avoids the whole line.

name: Halloween Gambit
description: A shock piece sacrifice that grabs a big pawn centre and open lines in exchange for the knight — a scary practical weapon at fast time controls.
recommended_response: 4...Nxe5 5.d4 is the main test; Black just needs to develop calmly and consolidate the extra piece.

name: Vienna Gambit
description: A King's Gambit in spirit, reached via the Vienna move order — trades a pawn for rapid development and kingside attacking chances.
recommended_response: 3...d5 strikes the centre at once and is the most direct, reliable equaliser.

name: Wing Gambit
description: Offers a queenside pawn against the Sicilian to open the b-file and swing pieces quickly toward the centre and kingside.
recommended_response: 2...cxb4 3.a3 (or 3.d4) accepts the pawn; 2...d5 simply ignores the offer and strikes the centre.

name: Göring Gambit
description: A Scotch Gambit relative that offers a second pawn for a big centre and a fast, natural lead in piece development.
recommended_response: 4...dxc3 5.Nxc3 (or 5.Bc4) accepts and returns the pawn later for comfortable development; 4...d5 declines directly.

name: Elephant Gambit
description: An early countergambit that hands over a pawn to seize the centre and free Black's pieces immediately.
recommended_response: 3.exd5 e4 4.Qe2 (or the simple 4.Nd4) is considered a safe, comfortable edge for White.

name: Latvian Gambit
description: One of the sharpest and riskiest replies to 1.e4 e5 — Black gambles a pawn immediately for wide-open, double-edged play.
recommended_response: 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 (or the simpler 3.Bc4) both leave White comfortably better with careful play.

name: Blumenfeld Gambit
description: Sacrifices a queenside pawn to build a strong pawn centre with ...e6/...d6 (or ...exd5) and active piece play.
recommended_response: 5.dxe6 fxe6 (or 5.Bg5) are the main tries; declining with 5.Bg5 keeps the position calmer.

name: Légal Trap
description: A 300-year-old queen sacrifice trap: if Black gets greedy and pins the knight without care, 5.Nxe5! offers the queen and mates with the two bishops and the other knight.
recommended_response: 4...Nc6 or 4...Nf6 develop safely; the trap only springs after a careless ...g6 or a hasty capture on d1.

name: Fishing Pole Trap
description: Black dangles a knight on g4 as bait — if White bites with the natural-looking Bxg4, ...h5! traps the bishop and Black comes out on top.
recommended_response: 9.h3 sidesteps the whole trap by asking the question before the knight ever gets to g4.

name: Traxler Counterattack
description: Instead of the normal 4...d5, Black ignores the attack on f7 entirely and counterattacks — one of the wildest, most forcing lines in all of open-game theory.
recommended_response: 5.Nxf7 or 5.Bxf7+ both lead to enormous complications either side can misplay; 5.d4!? is the calmer try.

name: Cochrane Gambit
description: White gives up a knight on move four of the Petrov to rip open Black's king early and grab a permanent grip on the centre and the bishop pair.
recommended_response: 4...Kxf7 is forced; 5.d4 (or 5.Nc3) keeps the initiative going without rushing the follow-up.

name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
description: A dubious-looking knight hop that punishes greed hard: if White grabs the e5 pawn, ...Qg5 forks the g2 pawn and the bishop on c4.
recommended_response: 4.Nxe5?? Qg5! wins material for Black; 4.O-O or 4.c3 simply ignores the trick and keeps White's edge.

name: Fajarowicz Gambit
description: A sharper cousin of the Budapest Gambit — instead of the standard ...Ng4, the knight jumps straight to e4 for immediate piece activity over the pawn.
recommended_response: 4.Nf3 or 4.a3 (ruling out ...Bb4+) both meet the knight's activity calmly and keep the extra pawn.

name: Portuguese Gambit
description: In the Scandinavian, Black delays recapturing the pawn again and pins the knight instead, banking on rapid development to outweigh the pawn deficit.
recommended_response: 4.f3 (bumping the bishop) or 4.Be2 both return the extra tempo for a safe, comfortable edge.

name: Parham Attack
description: An early queen sortie eyeing e5 and f7 — objectively nothing special, but it forces Black to respond precisely from move two or fall into real trouble.
recommended_response: 2...Nc6 is simplest; 2...g6 also works but requires knowing 3.Qf3! is met by 3...Nf6, not a careless developing move.

name: Milner-Barry Gambit
description: In the French Advance, White offers the d4 pawn to finish development a tempo faster and throw everything at Black's king before it can castle safely.
recommended_response: 5...cxd4 6.cxd4 Bd7 accepts and heads for the main tabiya; declining with 5...Qb6 first is also well tested.

name: Frankenstein-Dracula Variation
description: Black's pawn grab in the Vienna Game looks free, but 4.Qh5! immediately threatens mate and material — one of the wildest, most theory-dense forcing lines in the whole open game.
recommended_response: 4...Nd6 is the only move that survives the coming complications intact; anything else risks getting mated on the spot.

name: Grob's Attack
description: The most disreputable-looking first move in serious chess — objectively poor, but it takes the game so far out of book on move one that most opponents are on their own immediately.
recommended_response: 1...d5 or 1...e5 both punish the weakened kingside directly and give Black a comfortable, healthy game.

name: Icelandic Gambit
description: Black offers a second pawn in the Scandinavian complex to blow the position open before White's extra material can matter.
recommended_response: 4.dxe6 Bxe6 heads into a well-known tabiya; 4.d4 declines and holds onto the extra pawn.
